You are a JavaScript engineer. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (detached at HEAD). Edit files here directly. NEVER git commit, never touch /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself, NEVER call a model, NEVER use the network, NEVER run playwright, `npm run test:e2e` or the bench. FIRST run: [ -e frontend/node_modules ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/frontend/node_modules frontend/node_modules . Run tests with `cd frontend && node --test e2e/package-clock.test.js e2e/canon-policy.test.js e2e/blind-player.test.js`.

BACKGROUND. `loadPackagePacing({ storyId, repoRoot, pacingPath })` in `frontend/e2e/package-clock.js` returns a pacing projection (`sceneOrder`, `scenePoint(scene, "min"|"nudge"|"handoff")`, `eventOrder`, `eventPoint(id)`, `isConditional(id)`, `storyId`). It reads `data/stories/<story-id-with-dashes>/pacing.yaml`. That file no longer exists for the real story: commit 1ef50250 flipped `data/stories/continuity-initiative/` to a compiled source tree and moved the old file to `tests/fixtures/parity/continuity-initiative/legacy/pacing.yaml`. So `loadPackagePacing({ storyId: "continuity_initiative" })` throws ENOENT, which kills the hosted blind-player test (`blind-player.spec.js:122`) and `canon-policy.test.js` ("does not require transfer_window_1c after the real 1C early exit"). Read `package-clock.js`, `package-clock.test.js` and `canon-policy.test.js` first.

THE NEW SOURCE LAYOUT (read it, do not edit it). `data/stories/continuity-initiative/source/story.yaml` has `scenes:` (the scene order, a list of ids such as 1A to 3C). Each `source/scenes/<ID>.yaml` has `scene: <ID>`, `turns: {min, nudge, handoff}` (integers) and `beats:` (a list of pacing events with `id`, `at_turn` and an optional `when` mapping or list; a beat with a non-empty `when` is conditional). Python compiles these in `storygame/story_source/c_scene.py` (`build_pacing_scene`, `build_events`; read them for exact field meaning) and `storygame.story_package.loader.load_story_package(Path("data/stories/continuity-initiative"))` returns the compiled package whose `.pacing` has `scenes` (scene_id, min_turns, nudge_after_turns, handoff_after_turns) and `events` (id, scene_id, at_turn, when). `build_events` passes events through `apply_scene_order`, so the event order Python reports may differ from file order if a scene has an `order` entry for pacing events: find out and match Python's order.

BUILD. Keep the legacy `pacing.yaml` path working exactly as it is (the existing fixture tests depend on it, including every error message). Add a second source: when no `pacingPath` is given and `data/stories/<dashed-id>/pacing.yaml` does not exist but `data/stories/<dashed-id>/source/story.yaml` does, build the SAME projection from the source tree: scene order from `story.yaml` `scenes:`, each scene's turn points from its `turns` block, events from each scene's `beats` in scene order (then Python's event order, see above), `conditional` true when `when` is non-empty. Validate with the same rules and the same style of `pacingError` messages as the legacy path (turn points ordered min <= nudge <= handoff, non-negative safe integers, duplicate and undeclared scene ids, an `at_turn` past the scene's handoff, a missing `turns` block). Reuse the existing validation code instead of copying it: the cleanest shape is to normalise both inputs into the same intermediate lists (scenes with min/nudge/handoff, events with id/scene_id/at/when) and share the code that builds the projection. Use the `yaml` package already imported; add no dependency. A missing source tree still fails with the existing ENOENT-style error naming the legacy path.

TESTS in `package-clock.test.js` (no network): build a small fixture source tree in a tmp dir (a story.yaml with two scenes, two scene files with `turns` and a conditional and an unconditional beat) and assert the projection (order, points, event points, conditional); one failing case per validation rule above; legacy `pacing.yaml` still wins when both exist and when `pacingPath` is given; and one test against the REAL repo tree: `loadPackagePacing({ storyId: "continuity_initiative", repoRoot })` has scene order 1A,1B,1C,2A,2B,2C,3A,3B,3C, `scenePoint("1A","handoff").target_turn === 15`, and `eventOrder[0] === "kristin_steadies_1a"`. All three test files named above must pass.

HARD LIMITS. Edit only the two files above. Never edit anything under `data/`, `storygame/`, `tests/`, `factory/`, `bench/`, or any other frontend file, and add no dependencies. Write NOTES_15B_PACING.txt (worktree root, never committed) listing every ambiguity and your choice.

set -eo pipefail
WORK=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-station7-pacing
mkdir -p "$WORK/out"
[ -e frontend/node_modules ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/frontend/node_modules frontend/node_modules
[ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv

bad=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -vxF -e frontend/e2e/package-clock.js -e frontend/e2e/package-clock.test.js || true)
[ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "files outside ownership staged: $bad"; exit 1; }
cd frontend
start=$(date +%s)
node --test e2e/package-clock.test.js e2e/canon-policy.test.js e2e/blind-player.test.js e2e/merge-blind-player.test.js
took=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))
echo "node tests took $took s (budget 30 s)"
[ "$took" -le 30 ] || { echo "node tests over the 30 s budget"; exit 1; }
cd ..
# independent probe: Python's compiled pacing must equal the JS projection on the REAL story
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp
.venv/bin/python - > "$WORK/out/pacing-py.json" <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
from storygame.story_package.loader import load_story_package
p = load_story_package(Path("data/stories/continuity-initiative")).pacing
print(json.dumps({
    "scenes": [[s.scene_id, s.min_turns, s.nudge_after_turns, s.handoff_after_turns] for s in p.scenes],
    "events": [[e.id, e.scene_id, e.at_turn, bool(e.when)] for e in p.events],
}))
PY
cd frontend
node --input-type=module - > "$WORK/out/pacing-js.json" <<'JS'
import { loadPackagePacing } from "./e2e/package-clock.js";
const p = loadPackagePacing({ storyId: "continuity_initiative" });
const scenes = p.sceneOrder.map((id) => [id, p.scenePoint(id, "min").target_turn, p.scenePoint(id, "nudge").target_turn, p.scenePoint(id, "handoff").target_turn]);
const events = p.eventOrder.map((id) => { const e = p.eventPoint(id); return [id, e.scene_id, e.target_turn, p.isConditional(id)]; });
console.log(JSON.stringify({ scenes, events }));
JS
cd ..
cmp "$WORK/out/pacing-py.json" "$WORK/out/pacing-js.json" || { echo "JS pacing differs from Python's compiled pacing (py vs js above)"; head -c 600 "$WORK/out/pacing-py.json"; echo; head -c 600 "$WORK/out/pacing-js.json"; exit 1; }
echo "probe ok: JS pacing equals Python pacing ($(wc -c < "$WORK/out/pacing-js.json") bytes)"
git diff --cached > "$WORK/out/pacing.patch"
test -s "$WORK/out/pacing.patch"
